EmailTemplate.subject: Black Excellence: Make hosting a blood drive a part of your legacy this February
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Hi <Name> hope this email finds you well. As a Blood Program Leader, I am writing to propose a meaningful and impactful way your <school/church/org> can honor Black History Month in February.
Black History Month is a time to celebrate the rich heritage and contributions of African Americans to our society, while also making a positive difference in our communities. I would like to suggest organizing a blood drive as a way to both celebrate legacies during Black History Month and save lives.
Do you know Dr. Charles R. Drew? Dr. Charles R. Drew was an African American surgeon, educator and scientist who laid the groundwork for today’s modern blood donation program through his innovative work in blood banking. The Red Cross blood program started in 1940, under the leadership of Dr. Drew, who became the first medical director for the Red Cross in 1941.
Many schools, churches, and organizations like yours will soon begin planning activities and community projects soon, so let’s begin conversations for incorporating a blood drive to commemorate Black History Month and bring the community together.
Please let me know if you’re on board with hosting a Red Cross blood drive during Black History Month to honor the legacy and significant contributions of African Americans in our society.
Sincerely,
<AM/SAM/ABM Name>
